verdict.rationale: Lium is a GPU rental marketplace, so asking whether it offers a managed scheduler is a fair question. Its clusters feature provides several whole machines on one RDMA fabric for a distributed job, but that is raw nodes, not a managed scheduler. Nothing in the evidence mentions managed Slurm, Kubernetes, or any job queue or scheduler. The CLI and SDK run-and-remove features are one-off pod executions, which count only as adjacent features.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can schedule jobs on managed Slurm or Kubernetes instead of building my own scheduler on raw nodes
